column1: Per-negative-class accuracy on the T15 test set
column2: 0.6-clustering retrain (967 positives vs 2351 negatives). Four models. Hardest class first per model.
Number of windows of this negative class in the T15 test set.
Median of the model's 0-1 promoter score over the class. For a negative, lower is better: the model is more confident it is not a promoter.

Fraction of the class the model correctly scored BELOW the 0.5 cutoff (its true-negative rate for the class at the 0.5 threshold). Higher is better. Threshold-DEPENDENT: a model whose scores sit systematically higher (CNN-v2) rejects fewer here even when its ranking is good. Will shift after T26 calibration.

Probability the model scores a random real promoter above a random window of this class. 1.0 = perfectly separable, 0.5 = chance. Threshold-free and unchanged by calibration, so it is the fairer cross-model comparison.
90% bootstrap confidence interval for the AUROC (200 resamples).

column1: SRS is the diagnostic class: it is composition-matched (identical base and dinucleotide content, motif destroyed), so separability there can only come from the promoter MOTIF, not base/GC composition.

By SRS AUROC (motif learning): CNN-v2 0.924 > ProkBERT 0.906 > NT-LoRA 0.896 = CNN 0.896. CNN-v2's best-in-class SRS score is the strongest evidence any model here learned real motif signal rather than an AT-content shortcut.
CDS is the easiest class for every model (AUROC 0.925-0.980); the structured genomic negatives are more separable than SRS, as expected.
Overall correct-rejection rate across all 2351 negatives: NT-LoRA 0.915 > CNN 0.873 > ProkBERT 0.862 > CNN-v2 0.766.

CNN-v2's low overall rejection@0.5 is a CALIBRATION effect (its scores sit high), NOT weak discrimination: its per-class AUROCs are among the best. The rank-percentile ensemble (T29) is calibration-invariant, so this does not hurt CNN-v2 as an ensemble member.
Balanced test AUPRC (context): ProkBERT 0.884 > NT-LoRA 0.854 > CNN-v2 0.848 > CNN 0.804.
Source: modular_eval.py on the 0.6 T22 predictions (results/T25b/modular_eval.{md,csv}).
